answer: Let the required live bond scale with how fast an identity claims reward: draw winnings slowly and the kernel of stake you keep posted stays small; try to extract quickly and the bond curves up to swallow the gain. An honest agent earns at a patient, timber-steady pace and locks little. A farm wants its thousand heads to cash out fast, but each head's acceleration raises its own posted bond past the reward, so haste becomes the costly signal that prices the farm out. Slow honest earning is cheap; farm-speed extraction is self-defeating.
